extracted.intended_audience: Owners and drivers of General Motors vehicles (affected by Takata airbag inflators), GM dealerships/service centers, and the general public
extracted.subtask_description: Corporate/public safety recall communication informing vehicle owners about a defect, listing affected vehicles, explaining risks, and instructing owners how to obtain a free remedy. Aimed at ensuring owners are notified, understand urgency, and can access repair resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of commitment to safety
rubrics_metrics.description: At General Motors, we’re committed to your safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with a clear pledge of commitment to safety to build trust and frame the recall as an owner-focused safety action; offer help and resources (e.g., 'this website can help you understand the Takata airbag recall and what you should do').

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear technical explanation of defect and associated risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the defect and hazard in plain language: 'the propellant in the inflators may degrade after long-term exposure to high humidity and temperature cycling, which could cause the inflator to explode during a deployment... an inflator rupture may cause sharp metal fragments... which may result in injury or death.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe mechanism, environmental triggers, and possible consequences so owners understand severity and why action is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit list of affected vehicles and model years
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a detailed list of makes, models and model years affected (e.g., '2007–2014 Chevrolet Silverado 2500/3500 HD', '2003–2010 Pontiac Vibe', etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a comprehensive roster and encourage VIN lookup (link to my.gm.com/recalls) so owners can confirm whether their vehicle is involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide an immediate 'urgent' advisory when warranted
rubrics_metrics.description: Label critical cases clearly: 'Urgent Action Required' and specific 'DO NOT DRIVE' advisories for particularly hazardous vehicles (e.g., certain 2003-2004 Pontiac Vibe vehicles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When risk is high, give unambiguous instructions (do not drive), explain why, and offer immediate options (towing, loaner vehicles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer free repair and state repair availability
rubrics_metrics.description: State that affected vehicles 'are repaired for FREE' and list where repairs can be completed (e.g., 'at any one of over 4,100 General Motors dealership locations').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear the remedy is free-of-charge, specify eligible service locations/brands, and note any exceptions or special arrangements (Saab owners can use Saab Official Service Centers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide easily accessible how-to and logistics for repair
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell owners how to find a dealer, check vehicle status, and schedule repairs ('Check My Vehicle', 'You can have your FREE repair completed at any one of over 4,100...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include VIN lookup, links, and steps; mention courtesy transportation, extended appointment hours, and ask owners to contact dealers for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: List contact channels and phone numbers with accessibility support
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide Customer Assistance Center phone numbers, a central recall hotline (e.g., 1-866-467-9700), and TTY numbers for each brand and region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer multiple contact options (phone, TTY, links) and list numbers for specific brands/regions (Puerto Rico, Virgin Islands) to accommodate accessibility and language needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple outreach channels to notify owners
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure owners are aware through 'direct mailings, emails, live phone calls, automated phone calls, text messages, online messaging and special events.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ a multimodal contact strategy and invite owners to provide contact information (GM Owner Center) to improve reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner with external entities to locate and notify drivers
rubrics_metrics.description: Notify drivers by partnering with the Department of Motor Vehicles in select states, GM Dealerships, and GM entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborate with government and industry partners to increase notification reach and to identify vehicles in transition of ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search for affected vehicles for sale and intervene pre-resale
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with online used car listing services to find affected vehicles that are for sale and reach out to the seller to arrange repair prior to resale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively identify and contact sellers to prevent transfer of unrepaired vehicles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurately track scrapped or salvaged vehicles
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the National Motor Vehicle Title Information System to identify vehicles that are 'out of transit' and track those that have been scrapped or salvaged and are off the road.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage national title systems to maintain an accurate inventory of affected vehicles and their status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use online advertising to reach affected owners
rubrics_metrics.description: Make owners aware of the urgent safety recall by serving up online advertising to affected owners when they are engaging online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted digital ads can supplement direct outreach to reach owners who might not respond to mail or calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bring repairs to owners (mobile/home/work repairs)
rubrics_metrics.description: In select markets, work with a third-party mobile repair entity that allows owners to have their vehicles repaired for FREE at home, work or other convenient locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer mobile repair options to increase convenience and uptake, especially for owners who cannot easily visit a dealer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generate awareness at independent repair facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide display and shop communications so smaller, independent repair facilities can alert customers (materials to be posted in waiting areas and employee areas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target independent shops because owners of older models may service vehicles there and miss dealership notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use personalized live calls to help owners schedule repairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Launch live phone call pilot programs where agents provide personalized service, explain urgency, and schedule FREE appointments; agents work closely with dealers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personalized outreach can increase scheduling and completion rates; provide agents with dealer coordination capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve parts logistics and distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Get parts closer to where they are needed (parts nationwide at GM Parts Distribution Centers so dealers get parts quickly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimize parts distribution to reduce wait times and accelerate repairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-engage owners who showed prior interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-engage with owners who recently searched their VIN on GM Owner Center or engaged with outbound email communications, providing additional support and service scheduling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow up with previously engaged owners to convert interest into completed repairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirm or update owner contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm or update owner information whenever possible by including a Customer Feedback section in GM communications to give owners the opportunity to update their information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collecting updated contact data improves future recall outreach and owner contactability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop dealer-focused communications program
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a program to send dealer communications to affected owners using the dealers’ own format and contact information where available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage dealer-local formats and contact data to increase trust and response rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple data sources to find better contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Use multiple data sources, including physical address, email address and phone number; 'GM continues to look for "best-in-class" data so we can contact owners effectively.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate diverse data sources to maximize successful owner contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canvassing / door-to-door outreach in select markets
rubrics_metrics.description: Go door to door to contact owners through canvassing efforts in select markets to let them know that their vehicle is affected and to schedule a FREE recall repair immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use in-person canvassing where other channels fail or in targeted high-risk areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a comprehensive FAQ addressing common owner concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Frequently Asked Questions covering: which vehicles are subject to the recall; whether GM will execute the recall in stages; dealer hours during pandemic; how to check VIN; what to do if vehicle has the recall; where to complete recall repair; how to learn more; and reasons for 'Do Not Drive' advisories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate and answer common questions, including logistics, safety rationale, and special circumstances (e.g., pandemic-related dealer hours).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide language and regional accessibility support
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer content and assistance in multiple languages and list region-specific phone numbers (e.g., Puerto Rico English/Spanish numbers, Virgin Islands number) and TTY numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure non-English speakers and those needing TTY have clear access to recall information and assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with regulatory authorities and provide official resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate remedy activity with NHTSA, provide NHTSA videos and links, and state that GM has provided the remedy plan to NHTSA as requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference and link to regulatory agencies to provide authoritative context and additional resources for owners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe recall execution cadence and remedy planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain that, given a large population, GM 'will move in a cadenced way to replace inflators' and has coordinated the remedy plan with NHTSA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set expectations about the pace and stages of remedying vehicles and explain coordination with regulators to reassure owners about planning and safety oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize convenience measures for affected owners
rubrics_metrics.description: List convenience measures such as vehicle towing, loaner vehicles, courtesy transportation, and extended appointment hours to encourage prompt repair ('vehicle towing, and a loaner vehicle or other alternate transportation may be available for FREE').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer or highlight supportive services to remove barriers to getting the repair completed promptly.
